[3] There may be intense media interest, given the matter involves Kim Dotcom
against the background of his recent, but unrelated high-profile proceedings.1 While
there is public interest in the respondents’ identity and (perhaps) the facts of this matter,
there is little public interest in the applicant’s identity.
[4] Wide publication of VLN’s identity is likely to cause lasting harm to them
working in their chosen field or more widely. VLN might also be subject to hostile on-
line commentary, which I accept they are poorly placed to cope with.
[5] At this stage, I am satisfied that there are appropriate grounds to make an
exception to the principle of open justice. Pending further order, I prohibit the
publication of VLN’s name or their identifying particulars.
Employment relationship problem - file number 3459484
[6] VLN was engaged between late January/early February until late March 2026
by Contractors Only Limited and provided services at properties associated with Kim
Dotcom and Elizabeth Dotcom.
[7] In April 2026, VLN lodged an application in the Authority seeking a
determination that they were an employee of Kim Dotcom and Elizabeth Dotcom, as a
homeworker and/or because of the real nature of the relationship between them.2 If
VLN was an employee, they claimed personal grievances, unpaid wages and minimum
statutory entitlements. Alternatively, if Contractors Only Limited was VLN’s
employer, they sought orders under Part 9A of the Employment Relations Act 2000
against Elizabeth Dotcom that she was a person involved in breaches of employment
standards and liable for any default in payment by the employer.
[8] The statement of problem (file number 3459484) was served on Contractors
Only Limited and sent to both Elizabeth Dotcom and Kim Dotcom. The respondents
have not lodged a statement in reply.
[9] The Authority has not yet investigated this matter.
1 Dotcom v Minister of Justice [2026] NZCA 284.
2 Employment Relations Act 200 s 6(2).

3
Removal application – file number 3480646
[10] On 22 July 2026, VLN applied to remove the whole of the matter under file
number 3459484 to the Employment Court without the Authority investigating it. VLN
also sought urgency for the removal application.
[11] When the removal application was placed before me, I assigned urgency to it
and made directions regarding service of the removal application. I also abridged time
for the respondents to reply.
[12] I am satisfied that VLN and the Authority served the application in accordance
with the directions.
[13] The respondents have not lodged a statement in reply or otherwise engaged with
the Authority.
[14] VLN asks that the matter be decided on the papers. I am satisfied it is
appropriate to do so.
Grounds for removal
[15] The Authority has power to remove a matter to the Court in defined
circumstances.3 Here, VLN relies on the case being of such a nature and of such
urgency that it is in the public interest that it be removed immediately to the Court.
[16] VLN points to the recent judgment of the Court of Appeal dismissing Mr
Dotcom’s appeal against a High Court judgment. The High Court had earlier declined
Mr Dotcom’s application for judicial review of a Minister’s decision that he should be
surrendered for extradition to another jurisdiction. VLN’s submission is that their case
will be significantly affected to their disadvantage if Mr Dotcom is extradited before
their case can be finally decided.
[17] Relevant too is that the claim involves minimum employment standards,
assuming that VLN is found to be an employee. I note that part of the claim might be
prevented by the recent amendment to section 6 of the Employment Relations Act 2000
and the effect of transitional provisions contained in Schedule 1AA. However,
employment standards are potentially at issue prior to 21 February 2026. There is a
3 Employment Relations Act 2000 s 178(2).

4
public interest is resolving at least that part of VLN’s problem without it being
frustrated by the departure from New Zealand of Mr Dotcom.
[18] There is merit in these submissions. At this point, file number 3459484 has not
been progressed to an investigation by the Authority. There is little prospect of finally
resolving the claims in short order. The situation is within that contemplated by the
Employment Court in Jackson v The Aorere College Board of Trustees.4
[19] I am satisfied that grounds exist for the whole matter to be removed to the
Employment Court without the Authority investigating it.
Conclusion and orders
[20] On VLN’s application I order the removal of the whole of file number 3459484
to the Employment Court.
[21] Costs are reserved. If VLN seeks costs, they should lodge and serve a
memorandum within 28 days. The respondents must lodge and serve a reply within a
further 14 days. Costs will be determined based on the papers.
Philip Cheyne
Member of the Employment Relations Authority
4 Jackson v The Aorere College Board of Trustees [2012] NZEmpC 109; and see also Hendy v Vice-
